page:
- Secure Headers Middleware: simplifies setting HTTP security headers, inspired by Helmet; lets you enable/disable/override individual headers
- Import: `import { Hono } from 'hono'`, `import { secureHeaders } from 'hono/secure-headers'`
- Usage: `app.use(secureHeaders())` for optimal defaults; set an option to `false` to suppress a header (e.g. `xFrameOptions: false`); set a string to override a value (e.g. `strictTransportSecurity: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload'`)
- Removes the `X-Powered-By` header by default
- Supported options/headers: `contentSecurityPolicy`, `contentSecurityPolicyReportOnly`, `trustedTypes`, `requireTrustedTypesFor`, `crossOriginEmbedderPolicy` (default false), `crossOriginResourcePolicy`, `crossOriginOpenerPolicy`, `originAgentCluster`, `referrerPolicy`, `reportingEndpoints`, `reportTo`, `strictTransportSecurity`, `xContentTypeOptions`, `xDnsPrefetchControl`, `xDownloadOptions`, `xFrameOptions`, `xPermittedCrossDomainPolicies`, `xXssProtection`, `permissionPolicy`
- Middleware registration order affects header conflicts (e.g. secureHeaders vs poweredBy for x-powered-by)
- Supports CSP directives (defaultSrc, scriptSrc, etc.), a `NONCE` import for nonce attributes via `c.get('secureHeadersNonce')`, and custom nonce generator functions
- Supports Permissions-Policy configuration (fullscreen, bluetooth, payment, camera, microphone, geolocation, usb, accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer)
- Questions answered: How do I add security headers in Hono? How do I disable a header like X-Frame-Options? How do I set a Content-Security-Policy or a nonce? How do I configure Permissions-Policy? What are the default header values?

sections.manifest:
- Import statements for Secure Headers Middleware
- `import { Hono } from 'hono'`
- `import { secureHeaders } from 'hono/secure-headers'`
- Answers: How do I import the Secure Headers Middleware?

- Shows three usage patterns for Secure Headers Middleware
- Default optimal settings: `app.use(secureHeaders())`
- Suppressing headers by setting them to `false`: `secureHeaders({ xFrameOptions: false, xXssProtection: false })`
- Overriding header values with strings: `secureHeaders({ strictTransportSecurity: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload', xFrameOptions: 'DENY', xXssProtection: '1' })`
- Applied with `app.use('*', secureHeaders({...}))`
- Answers: How do I enable default secure headers? How do I disable a specific header? How do I override a header's value with a custom string?

- Table mapping each option to its Header, Value, and Default (True/False/No Setting)
- `X-Powered-By` header is always deleted by default (no option name; Default: True)
- `contentSecurityPolicy`, `contentSecurityPolicyReportOnly`, `trustedTypes`, `requireTrustedTypesFor`, `reportingEndpoints`, `reportTo`, `permissionPolicy`: no default setting, usage documented separately
- `crossOriginEmbedderPolicy` -> `require-corp`, default **False**
- `crossOriginResourcePolicy` -> `same-origin`, default True
- `crossOriginOpenerPolicy` -> `same-origin`, default True
- `originAgentCluster` -> `?1`, default True
- `referrerPolicy` -> `no-referrer`, default True
- `strictTransportSecurity` -> `max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains`, default True
- `xContentTypeOptions` -> `nosniff`, default True
- `xDnsPrefetchControl` -> `off`, default True
- `xDownloadOptions` -> `noopen`, default True
- `xFrameOptions` -> `SAMEORIGIN`, default True
- `xPermittedCrossDomainPolicies` -> `none`, default True
- `xXssProtection` -> `0`, default True
- Answers: What is the default value of X-Frame-Options? Which headers are enabled by default? What does crossOriginEmbedderPolicy default to? What is the default Strict-Transport-Security value?

- Explains header conflicts when multiple middleware manipulate the same header, and the importance of registration order
- Example: `app.use(secureHeaders()); app.use(poweredBy())` — secureHeaders operates and `x-powered-by` is removed
- Example: `app.use(poweredBy()); app.use(secureHeaders())` — Powered-By operates and `x-powered-by` is added
- Answers: Does middleware order matter when combining secureHeaders and poweredBy middleware? How do I make sure X-Powered-By is removed? What happens if I register poweredBy before secureHeaders?

- Full example of configuring `contentSecurityPolicy` via `secureHeaders()` scoped to the path `/test`
- Shows a `reportingEndpoints` array (name/url) as an alternative to `reportTo`
- CSP directives shown: `defaultSrc`, `baseUri`, `childSrc`, `connectSrc`, `fontSrc`, `formAction`, `frameAncestors`, `frameSrc`, `imgSrc`, `manifestSrc`, `mediaSrc`, `objectSrc`, `reportTo`, `reportUri` (`/csp-report`), `sandbox`, `scriptSrc`, `scriptSrcAttr`, `scriptSrcElem`, `styleSrc`, `styleSrcAttr`, `styleSrcElem`, `upgradeInsecureRequests`, `workerSrc`
- `NONCE` attribute: import `NONCE` from `hono/secure-headers` and the `SecureHeadersVariables` type; add `NONCE` to `scriptSrc`/`styleSrc`; retrieve the value via `c.get('secureHeadersNonce')` to set the `nonce` attribute on `<script>` elements
- Custom nonce generator: define a `ContentSecurityPolicyOptionHandler` function (e.g. `myNonceGenerator`) called on every request, which sets a value via `c.set()` and returns `nonce-${nonce}`, used in place of `NONCE` in `scriptSrc`
- Answers: How do I configure Content-Security-Policy directives in Hono? How do I add a nonce to CSP script-src? How do I generate my own CSP nonce value? What is SecureHeadersVariables used for?

- Example configuring the `permissionsPolicy` option of `secureHeaders()`
- Directive value forms and resulting header syntax: `fullscreen: ['self']` -> `fullscreen=(self)`; `bluetooth: ['none']` -> `bluetooth=(none)`; `payment: ['self', 'https://example.com']` -> `payment=(self "https://example.com")`; `syncXhr: []` -> `sync-xhr=()`; `camera: false` -> `camera=none`; `microphone: true` -> `microphone=*`; `geolocation: ['*']` -> `geolocation=*`; `usb: ['self', 'https://a.example.com', 'https://b.example.com']` -> `usb=(self "https://a.example.com" "https://b.example.com")`; `accelerometer: ['https://*.example.com']` -> `accelerometer=("https://*.example.com")`; `gyroscope: ['src']` -> `gyroscope=(src)`; `magnetometer: ['https://a.example.com', 'https://b.example.com']` -> `magnetometer=("https://a.example.com" "https://b.example.com")`
- Answers: How do I set the Permissions-Policy header in Hono? How do I allow a feature for specific origins only? How do I disable a browser feature like camera or bluetooth via Permissions-Policy? What does an empty array mean for a permissions policy directive?
